report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Fixed deadline, defined scope, known technology stack (banking APIs, reconciliation logic), and explicit team composition drive a predictive approach despite extreme time pressure.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build an internal payment reconciliation platform integrating with Chase, Wells Fargo, and Stripe that performs automated three-way transaction matching, flags discrepancies, and generates SOX-compliant audit reports.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Finance team (25 people) and external auditors.
project_understanding.trigger: Regulatory audit scheduled in 3 weeks; current manual Excel-based reconciliation process is non-compliant with SOX requirements.
success_definition: 100% of transactions reconciled automatically within 24 hours
Discrepancy rate flagged for human review under 0.1%
SOX-compliant audit trail exportable as PDF and CSV
Integration live with all three banking partners (Chase, Wells Fargo, Stripe)
supporting_quotes: Regulatory audit is scheduled for 3 weeks from today
The CFO has stated this is non-negotiable — the audit cannot proceed without an automated trail
Timeline: 3 weeks hard deadline. No extensions possible.

hard_constraints.team_composition: 2 Backend Engineers, 1 Product Manager. No QA engineer budgeted.
hard_constraints.technology_stack: Banking APIs (Chase, Wells Fargo, Stripe), reconciliation engine, audit trail system. Stack not explicitly specified beyond integrations.
hard_constraints.compliance: SOX compliance required; audit trail must be exportable and regulatory-compliant

non_functional_requirements.performance: 100% of transactions reconciled within 24 hours (batch processing acceptable)
non_functional_requirements.availability: UNKNOWN — audit trail must be available for auditor access, but uptime SLA not specified
non_functional_requirements.security: SOX compliance implies authentication, authorization, encryption at rest and in transit, and immutable audit logging
non_functional_requirements.usability: UNKNOWN — UI/UX for discrepancy review not specified
non_functional_requirements.data_retention: UNKNOWN — how long audit trails and transaction records must be retained
non_functional_requirements.scalability: UNKNOWN — expected transaction volume not specified, but 25-person finance team suggests moderate scale

assumption_log.what: Availability SLA for audit trail access is 99.5% during business hours (standard for internal financial systems)
assumption_log.why: Auditors need reliable access to audit trail during audit window; no explicit SLA stated, so standard business-hours availability is reasonable default
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope baseline requires acceptance of quality characteristics
assumption_log.consequence: If actual availability requirement is 99.9% or 24/7, infrastructure architecture must change (redundancy, failover, monitoring); re-architecture required
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows infrastructure planning to proceed without stakeholder delay. Risks: if auditors require 24/7 access, deployment architecture must be redesigned mid-project.

assumption_log.what: Data retention requirement is 7 years (standard for SOX-regulated financial records)
assumption_log.why: SOX compliance typically requires 7-year retention; no explicit retention period stated in input
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires documented constraints
assumption_log.consequence: If actual retention is shorter (e.g., 3 years) or longer (e.g., indefinite), storage architecture and archival strategy must change; re-architecture required
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows database schema and archival design to proceed. Risks: if wrong, storage costs and compliance audit failure.

assumption_log.what: Expected transaction volume is 10,000–50,000 transactions per day across all three banking partners
assumption_log.why: Finance team of 25 people suggests mid-market company; no explicit volume stated. Assumption allows performance testing and database sizing to proceed.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope definition including performance constraints
assumption_log.consequence: If actual volume is 500,000+ transactions/day, database and reconciliation engine must be re-architected for scale; performance testing will fail late in Phase 3
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows database schema and reconciliation algorithm design to proceed. Risks: if volume is higher, Phase 3 integration testing will expose performance failures requiring re-architecture.

assumption_log.what: Banking partner APIs (Chase, Wells Fargo, Stripe) have sandbox environments available and documented; authentication is via API keys or OAuth; rate limits are at least 1,000 requests/minute
assumption_log.why: All three are major financial services providers with mature APIs; sandbox access is standard. No explicit API documentation or rate limits stated.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline
assumption_log.consequence: If sandbox access is unavailable, delayed, or requires legal approval, Phase 2 development cannot start. If rate limits are lower than assumed, reconciliation engine must be redesigned.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 2 development to start immediately. Risks: if API access is delayed or restricted, critical path is blocked.

assumption_log.what: SOX audit trail implementation requires immutable logging, role-based access control (RBAC), and cryptographic signing of audit records; no additional compliance frameworks (HIPAA, PCI-DSS) apply
assumption_log.why: SOX compliance is explicitly stated; immutable audit trail is standard SOX requirement. No other compliance frameworks mentioned.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope baseline requires acceptance of regulatory constraints
assumption_log.consequence: If PCI-DSS or other compliance frameworks apply, security architecture must expand; Phase 3 security review will fail and require re-architecture
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows security architecture to be scoped to SOX only. Risks: if additional compliance applies, security implementation will be incomplete.

project_plan.buffer_note: No buffer can be applied — deadline is fixed at 3 weeks with no extensions possible. This is a critical risk.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Every task is on the critical path with zero slack; any delay in any task cascades to project failure. Both backend engineers must be 100% allocated and cannot be interrupted. PM must be full-time for coordination and stakeholder management.

risk_register.description: If 3-week deadline is fixed and scope includes full integration with three banking partners plus SOX compliance, then critical path will exceed available time and project will fail to deliver before audit.
risk_register.trigger: Any task in Phase 1 or Phase 2 slips by more than 1 day; any banking partner API access delayed; any security review finding requires re-architecture
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm banking partner sandbox access and API documentation on Day 1 (T1); parallelize API connector development (T5, T6, T7 run simultaneously); pre-stage production infrastructure before Phase 5
risk_register.contingency: If any critical path task slips, immediately escalate to CFO and auditors to negotiate audit delay or scope reduction (e.g., defer one banking partner to post-audit phase)

risk_register.description: If only 2 backend engineers are allocated and both are on the critical path with zero slack, then any illness, context-switching, or competing priority will break the schedule.
risk_register.trigger: Either engineer unavailable for more than 1 day; either engineer pulled to another project; either engineer context-switches to support production issues
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from engineering leadership that both engineers are 100% allocated and cannot be interrupted; establish daily standup to detect blockers immediately; pre-identify backup engineer who can step in if needed
risk_register.contingency: If either engineer becomes unavailable, immediately escalate to VP Engineering and CFO; negotiate scope reduction or audit delay

risk_register.description: If banking partner APIs (Chase, Wells Fargo, Stripe) have undocumented rate limits, schema changes, or sandbox access delays, then Phase 2 development will be blocked.
risk_register.trigger: Sandbox access not granted within 24 hours; API documentation incomplete or contradicts actual behavior; rate limits lower than 1,000 req/min; API schema changes mid-project
risk_register.mitigation: Contact all three banking partners on Day 1 to confirm sandbox access and obtain API documentation; establish direct technical contact at each partner; test API connectivity before Phase 2 starts
risk_register.contingency: If any API access is delayed, immediately escalate to CFO and banking partner relationship manager; request expedited access or negotiate audit delay

risk_register.description: If SOX audit trail implementation is incomplete or does not meet auditor expectations, then audit will fail and project will not achieve success criteria.
risk_register.trigger: Auditors identify gaps in immutability, RBAC, or cryptographic signing during UAT; audit trail export format does not meet auditor requirements; compliance review identifies additional requirements (e.g., PCI-DSS)
risk_register.mitigation: Engage external auditors in Phase 1 to review audit trail design before implementation; include auditor sign-off in Phase 3 security review; test audit trail export format with auditors before Phase 4 UAT
risk_register.contingency: If auditors identify gaps in Phase 4, immediately escalate to CFO; negotiate scope reduction or audit delay

risk_register.description: If three-way matching algorithm does not achieve < 0.1% discrepancy rate on production data, then success criteria will not be met.
risk_register.trigger: Test data shows discrepancy rate > 0.1%; production data reveals edge cases not covered by algorithm (e.g., partial matches, timing drift); matching logic produces false positives
risk_register.mitigation: Design matching algorithm with explicit handling for partial matches and timing drift (T2); test algorithm on representative sample of historical transaction data before Phase 2; include finance team in algorithm validation
risk_register.contingency: If discrepancy rate exceeds threshold in Phase 3, immediately escalate to finance team; negotiate acceptable threshold or redesign algorithm (high risk of schedule slip)

risk_register.description: If no dedicated QA engineer is allocated and developers test their own code, then defect escape rate will be high and critical bugs will be discovered late in Phase 4.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 4 UAT discovers critical bugs (data loss, audit trail corruption, API failures); defect escape rate exceeds 10%; auditors identify compliance gaps in testing
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate minimum 25% of development effort to QA (currently 0%); hire contract QA engineer or reallocate one backend engineer to QA role; implement automated test suite for matching algorithm and audit trail; conduct security review in Phase 3 before Phase 4 UAT
risk_register.contingency: If critical bugs are discovered in Phase 4, immediately escalate to CFO; negotiate audit delay or scope reduction

risk_register.description: If Phase 4 (QA & Testing) is compressed to 15% of timeline (0.45 weeks = 2.7 days) with no dedicated QA engineer, then testing will be insufficient and defects will reach production.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 4 timeline is 2.7 calendar days; developers cannot complete both bug fixes and UAT in that window; auditors identify untested code paths during UAT
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate dedicated QA engineer to Phase 4 (minimum 25% of dev effort); implement automated test suite in Phase 2 to reduce manual testing burden; conduct security review in Phase 3 before Phase 4 UAT
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 4 timeline is insufficient, immediately escalate to CFO; negotiate audit delay or scope reduction

risk_register.description: If stakeholder expectations for audit trail completeness or discrepancy accuracy are not formally documented and signed off, then UAT will fail and project will not achieve success criteria.
risk_register.trigger: Finance team or auditors expect different discrepancy threshold (e.g., 0.05% instead of 0.1%); audit trail export format does not match auditor expectations; success criteria are interpreted differently by different stakeholders
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written sign-off from finance team and external auditors on success criteria in Phase 1 (T2); include auditors in algorithm design review; conduct UAT with both finance team and auditors present
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholders disagree on success criteria in Phase 4, immediately escalate to CFO; negotiate scope reduction or audit delay

risk_register.description: If transaction volume is higher than assumed (A3: 10,000–50,000/day), then database and reconciliation engine will not complete 24-hour reconciliation window and performance will fail.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 performance testing reveals reconciliation takes > 24 hours; production data volume exceeds 50,000 transactions/day; database queries timeout or lock
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain actual transaction volume estimate from finance team in Phase 1 (T4); conduct performance testing on production-scale data in Phase 3 (T11); design database schema with indexing strategy for expected volume
risk_register.contingency: If performance testing fails, immediately escalate to finance team; negotiate acceptable reconciliation window or scope reduction

risk_register.description: If $50,000 budget is insufficient for 3 backend engineers (2 allocated + 1 contract QA engineer) for 3 weeks, then project will run out of budget before completion.
risk_register.trigger: Contract QA engineer costs exceed budget; infrastructure costs (database, API calls, monitoring) exceed budget; overtime costs for schedule compression exceed budget
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain detailed cost estimate for contract QA engineer and infrastructure in Phase 1; negotiate fixed-price contract with QA provider; pre-stage production infrastructure to avoid last-minute costs
risk_register.contingency: If budget is exceeded, immediately escalate to CFO; negotiate budget increase or scope reduction

staffing_plan.notes: Must be 100% allocated and full-time. Responsible for stakeholder alignment, scope management, and escalation. Cannot be shared with other projects.
Must be 100% allocated and full-time. Owns API integrations, matching algorithm, and audit trail implementation. Cannot be shared with other projects. No backup identified — single point of failure.

RECOMMENDED ADDITION — not budgeted in input. Required to meet 25% QA effort minimum (PMBOK 8.2). Current plan allocates 0% QA effort, which violates QA staffing rule. Contract QA engineer must be hired immediately to conduct Phase 3 integration testing and Phase 4 UAT. Cost impact: ~$15,000–$20,000 (within $50,000 budget if other costs are controlled).

staffing_vs_stated_team_assumptions.what: QA Engineer (contract) will be available for Phases 3-4 at 15% allocation (80 hours total)
staffing_vs_stated_team_assumptions.why: Input specifies no QA engineer budgeted; developers will test their own code. However, PMBOK 8.2 requires QA effort to be minimum 25% of development effort. With 400 hours of development effort, minimum QA is 100 hours. Assuming contract QA engineer at 80 hours (20% of dev effort) is a compromise that partially addresses the gap but still falls short of the 25% minimum.
staffing_vs_stated_team_assumptions.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.2 — Quality Management Plan requires QA effort allocation
staffing_vs_stated_team_assumptions.consequence: If contract QA engineer is unavailable or budget does not allow hiring, QA effort drops to 0% (developer self-testing only). Defect escape rate will be high; critical bugs will be discovered in Phase 4 UAT or production, causing schedule slip or audit failure.
staffing_vs_stated_team_assumptions.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 3-4 testing to be more rigorous than developer self-testing alone. Risks: if contract QA engineer is not hired, QA effort remains insufficient and defect escape rate will be high.

project_viability.gap_amount: Critical path duration is 15 days (3 weeks calendar time); timeline is at absolute minimum with zero slack. Budget of $50,000 is insufficient for 3 backend engineers + 1 contract QA engineer for 3 weeks (estimated cost: $60,000–$75,000 including infrastructure and contingency).

scoping_options.description: Reduce scope to single banking partner (e.g., Chase only) for initial audit; defer Wells Fargo and Stripe integrations to post-audit phase 2
scoping_options.impact: Reduces Phase 2 development effort by ~40%; frees 1 backend engineer for QA role; allows 24-hour reconciliation window to be met with single-partner data volume
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Audit will only cover Chase transactions; finance team must manually reconcile Wells Fargo and Stripe transactions until phase 2 completes. Auditors may not accept partial automation. Requires stakeholder re-approval.

scoping_options.description: Extend timeline to 5 weeks (add 2 weeks buffer); hire dedicated QA engineer; allocate 15% buffer to critical path tasks
scoping_options.impact: Allows proper QA allocation (25% of dev effort); reduces schedule risk from CRITICAL to HIGH; provides slack for integration testing and bug fixes
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Misses 3-week audit deadline; requires CFO and auditor approval for delay. May not be acceptable given regulatory pressure.

scoping_options.description: Hire 1 additional backend engineer (total 3) and 1 contract QA engineer; parallelize API connector development and matching algorithm work; compress timeline to 3 weeks with proper QA
scoping_options.impact: Allows full scope (all three banking partners) to be delivered in 3 weeks with dedicated QA; reduces schedule risk from CRITICAL to MEDIUM; increases cost to ~$75,000
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Budget increases by $25,000 (50% over stated $50,000); requires CFO approval for budget increase. Hiring and onboarding additional engineer in 24 hours is high-risk.

scoping_options.description: Accept developer self-testing (0% QA allocation); compress Phase 4 to 1 week; accept higher defect escape rate and audit risk
scoping_options.impact: Stays within 3-week timeline and $50,000 budget; delivers full scope
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Defect escape rate will be high; critical bugs will likely be discovered in production or during auditor review; audit may fail due to untested code paths or compliance gaps. NOT RECOMMENDED.

open_questions.question: Can the 3-week deadline be extended to 5 weeks, or is the regulatory audit date immovable? If immovable, can the audit scope be reduced to a single banking partner for the initial audit?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If deadline is truly immovable and scope cannot be reduced, project is not viable. Proceeding without answering this question will result in schedule failure and audit failure.

open_questions.question: What is the actual daily transaction volume across all three banking partners? Is it within the assumed 10,000–50,000 range, or significantly higher?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If volume is higher than assumed, Phase 3 performance testing will fail and reconciliation engine must be re-architected. This will cause schedule slip.

open_questions.question: Can the $50,000 budget be increased to $75,000 to hire a dedicated QA engineer and additional backend engineer? If not, which scope items should be deferred to post-audit phase 2?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If budget cannot be increased and QA engineer cannot be hired, QA effort will be 0% (developer self-testing only). Defect escape rate will be high and audit will likely fail.

open_questions.question: Have the external auditors been engaged to review the SOX audit trail design and confirm that the planned implementation meets their requirements? If not, when can this review be scheduled?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If auditors identify gaps in audit trail design during Phase 4 UAT, re-architecture will be required and schedule will slip. Engaging auditors in Phase 1 is critical to avoid late-stage surprises.

open_questions.question: Have sandbox credentials and API documentation been obtained from Chase, Wells Fargo, and Stripe? If not, what is the expected timeline for access approval?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If sandbox access is delayed beyond Day 1, Phase 2 development will be blocked and critical path will slip. This is the highest-risk dependency.
